title: Base ionization constant, Kb

items.label: K_b
items.meaning: equilibrium constant for the ionization of a weak base in water (the base ionization constant); often reported as pK_b = -log K_b

items.label: [HB^+]
items.meaning: equilibrium concentration of the conjugate acid of the weak base (mol/L)

items.label: [B]
items.meaning: equilibrium concentration of the un-ionized weak base (mol/L)

caution: Applies to a solution of a weak base, which involves equilibrium between the un-ionized base and its conjugate acid; [OH^-] does not equal the initial base concentration. For any conjugate acid-base pair, K_w = K_a × K_b.

title: Weak base + strong acid: three cases
body: When a weak base and a strong acid are mixed they react quantitatively, B(aq) + H3O+(aq) ⇌ HB+(aq) + H2O(l), and the pH depends on which species is in excess or whether they are equimolar.

items.label: Weak base in excess
items.meaning: a buffer solution is formed; pH is determined from the Henderson-Hasselbalch (H-H) equation

items.label: Strong acid in excess
items.meaning: pH is determined from the moles of excess hydronium ion and the total volume of solution

items.label: Equimolar
items.meaning: the (slightly acidic) pH is determined from the equilibrium HB+(aq) + H2O(l) ⇌ B(aq) + H3O+(aq)

ced_evidence: 8.4.A.3: B(aq) + H3O+(aq) ⇌ HB+(aq) + H2O(l); weak base in excess → buffer, H-H equation; strong acid in excess → moles of excess hydronium ion and total volume; equimolar → (slightly acidic) pH from HB+(aq) + H2O(l) ⇌ B(aq) + H3O+(aq)

title: Titration curve (pH vs. volume of titrant)
body: A titration curve plots pH against the volume of titrant added and summarizes results from a titration; students read it to find the equivalence point and, for weak acids/bases, the half-equivalence point.

items.label: Equivalence point
items.meaning: moles of titrant added equal moles of analyte originally present (monoprotic acids or bases); pH is set by the major species present (neutral for strong acid-strong base; basic for a weak acid titration, acidic for a weak base titration)

items.label: Half-equivalence point
items.meaning: for a weak acid, the point halfway to the equivalence point where [HA] = [A−], so pH = pKa

caution: Do not confuse the half-equivalence point (pH = pKa) with the equivalence point; pKa is read from the pH at the half-equivalence point, not the equivalence point.
ced_evidence: 8.5.A.1 A titration curve, plotting pH against the volume of titrant added; 8.5.A.3 half-equivalence point, pH = pKa

title: Buffer solution
body: A buffer solution contains a large concentration of both members of a conjugate acid-base pair, so the conjugate acid reacts with added base and the conjugate base reacts with added acid, stabilizing pH.
ced_evidence: 8.8.A.1 A buffer solution contains a large concentration of both members in a conjugate acid-base pair; 8.4.A.3 buffer formed when the weak base is in excess

title: Henderson-Hasselbalch equation

items.label: pK_a
items.meaning: negative log of the acid ionization constant K_a of the weak acid (unitless)

items.label: [HA]
items.meaning: concentration of the conjugate acid (weak acid) (mol/L)

caution: Relates buffer pH to the pKa and the concentration ratio of the conjugate acid-base pair. Derivation of the equation and computation of the change in pH on adding acid or base to a buffer are not assessed on the AP Exam.
